text:
maria: quick sync — dropping a first-pass framing for the Optimize toolkit PRD + a tiny RFC for batching/caching/quant recs. goal: align on minimum launch scope and acceptance criteria by EOD friday.
vikram: thanks. can you call out which customer asks are in-scope vs. backlog? there are a few enterprise asks we should not accidentally scope in.
sam: re: enterprise asks — they want per-tenant cache isolation & audit logs. I think isolation is out for MVP but logging should be included.
elaine: agreed with sam. logging + cost breakdown per-route are high-value and low-effort. cache isolation is a Dedicated/private feature.
maria: provisional scope list: 1) batching heuristics + safe defaults; 2) prefix/KV cache toggle + TTL + stale policy; 3) quantization guidance + test harness for quality smoke checks; 4) rollout playbook (canary, fallback). not including per-tenant isolation or custom KMS integration.
juniper: for batching heuristics — do we ship both latency-first and throughput-first presets? or a single adaptive mode?
vikram: prefer: adaptive default (works for 95% of workloads) + two explicit presets (latency, throughput) for power users. acceptance criteria should include measurable gains: e.g., 10-20% lower cost or 30% better throughput on batchy workloads.
maria: proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
```
- default adaptive batching reduces mean tokens/sec cost by >=10% on benchmark suite A
- latency preset keeps median + tail latency within 5% of baseline for 95th pct requests
- KV cache reduces compute tokens by >=15% on conversational workloads with prefix reuse >=30%
- quantization guidance ties to a quality regression check: end-to-end generation BLEU/ROUGE drop <=1.5% vs FP16 for recommended quant profiles
- rollout plan: canary at 1% traffic + auto-fallback in 5min on error spike
- observability: per-route cost + token breakdown visible in console
```
sam: can we be more concrete on benchmark suite A? list of workloads + datasets?
maria: yes: a small set — convo-qa (open-domain chat), docs-summarize (long context), short-completion (low-latency), and batch-embedding workload. will attach specifics to PRD.
elaine: edge cases to call out in PRD: token cache invalidation when model version pinned; long-tail sequence length spikes breaking batching window; mixed model families where quant profiles differ.
juniper: also call out cross-region routing fallback: if preferred region is saturated, fallback to a cheaper-but-slower model variant, but we must preserve privacy constraints (no cross-region for Private customers).
maria: good catch — add constraints matrix in PRD.
vikram: mini-RFC question: quant recs should be per-model + per-workload. do we include automatic A/B quality checks during quant rollout or just guidance docs?
sam: we should include an automated smoke harness that runs a small eval set on the quantized variant during canary. if regression > threshold block rollout. low engineering cost and big risk reduction.
maria: ok action items: 1) vikram to draft adaptive batching algo + presets and add microbench code snippets by tomorrow @ 11am; 2) sam to spec the smoke harness + blocking thresholds; 3) juniper to enumerate edgecases and privacy constraints matrix; 4) elaine to draft observability rows (per-route cost, tokens, hit-rate). i'll assemble PRD + mini-RFC for quant and ping eng-ml for review.
ops-bot: reminder — weekly roadmap sync in #product tomorrow 9:30am.
maria: thanks all. if nobody objects I'll mark this scope frozen for the PRD and start writing acceptance tests. objections?
vikram: no objections from eng-ml side.
sam: no objections.
elaine: fine by me.
juniper: good to go.
maria: great — will post PRD link in thread when ready and open a 24-hr comment window before final sign-off.
